title: Average one-bit KL cost bounded by Alice's information term
statement:
Fix a positive integer $n$ and a deterministic communication protocol $p$ for set-disjointness, whose inputs are the pairs of subsets $X, Y \subseteq \{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$ produced by the hard distribution. Let $\mu$ be the hard distribution conditioned both on the two generated sets being disjoint and on Bob's bit $Y_T$ at the special coordinate $T$ being $\mathrm{false}$, and for a sample $\omega$ write $\Pi(\omega)$ for the transcript of $p$ run on the input pair $(X, Y)$ generated by $\omega$. Let $Z(\omega) = \big(\Pi(\omega),\, T,\, X_{<T},\, Y_{>T}\big)$ be the statistic recording the transcript, the special coordinate, Alice's bits strictly before $T$, and Bob's bits strictly after $T$. For each value $z$ that $Z$ can take, let $D(z)$ be the Kullback–Leibler divergence, from the uniform distribution on one bit, of the conditional law of Alice's special bit $X_T$ given $Z = z$, where the conditioning is taken with respect to the ambient uniform law on samples. Then
\[
  \int D\big(Z(\omega)\big)\, d\mu(\omega) \;\le\; \tfrac{3}{2}\, I\!\big(X_T \,;\, \Pi \,\big|\, T,\, X_{<T},\, Y_{\ge T}\big),
\]
where the conditional mutual information on the right is computed under the hard distribution conditioned only on the two generated sets being disjoint.
hypotheses_covered: n is a positive integer (instance length)
p is a deterministic protocol for length-n set-disjointness
the integration is against the hard distribution conditioned on disjointness and on Bob's special bit Y_T being false
the KL integrand compares the conditional law of X_T (under the ambient uniform sample law) against the uniform bit
Z is the statistic (transcript, T, X_{<T}, Y_{>T})
the mutual information conditions on (T, X_{<T}, Y_{>=T}) under the disjointness-conditioned distribution
caveat: The conditional law of X_T defining the KL integrand is formed against the ambient (uniform) sample measure via the Z-fiber, whereas the outer expectation and the mutual-information term use the disjointness-conditioned hard distribution; the prose keeps these base measures distinct. Note also that Z carries Y strictly after T (Y_{>T}) while the mutual information conditions on Y from T onward (Y_{>=T}), matching the Lean.
replaced: Alice information step under $D ∧ Y_{T}=false$: the average one-bit KL cost is bounded by Alice's information term, with the $2/3$ conditioning factor.
